policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'Jonathan loved him' renders a 3ms verb with 3ms object. The qere gives that plene; the ketiv ויאהבו is readable as the same form with a defectively written suffix. The English does not distinguish the spellings, and no note is mapped here.

ASV 'singing' matches the qere לשיר directly, but the ketiv לשור is readable as a variant spelling of the same infinitive 'to sing'. The English cannot separate the two orthographies; both verse notes are alternative_rendering and touch other words.

ASV 'his thousands' is plural, as the qere באלפיו spells it; the ketiv באלפו is the routine defective writing of the same plural suffix (ו for יו), not a distinct singular the English would exclude. The only note is alternative_rendering on 'sang one to another'.

ASV 'eyed' renders the participle 'eyeing' that the qere עוין spells plene; the ketiv עון is readable as the same participle written defectively. The English wording does not distinguish them and no note is mapped to this unit.
